summary: Alexander Meyrick Broadley worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied law at Lincoln's Inn from circa 1866 to 1869, and served in the Indian Civil Service as Assistant, then Collector, between 1869 and 1872.

Alexander Murray was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Edinburgh from circa 1794 to 1812, earning a D.D., and was appointed Professor of Oriental Languages there in 1812.

Alexander O. Hsu specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago Divinity School (circa 2011–2018), supervised by Paul Copp and Christian K. Wedemeyer, and later held a teaching position at North Dakota State University.

Alexander Piatigorsky worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Moscow State University, held research and teaching posts there and at the Russian Academy of Sciences, and later served as Professor of the Ancient History of South Asia at SOAS (1990–2001).

Alexander Potebnja was a linguist and philosopher who studied at the University of Kharkiv, earning his Ph.D., and under Albrecht Weber. He spent his career at the University of Kharkiv, serving as Professor in 1875.

Alexander Rea was a specialist in history, archaeology, and Indology. He built his career at the Archaeological Survey of India, serving as Assistant in 1882, head in 1886, and Superintendent from 1902 to 1913.

Alexander Robertson worked in religious studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Aberdeen, completing an M.A. circa 1894–1898, as well as the University of Glasgow, and served as a missionary with the United Free Church of Scotland (1902–1937).

Alexander Rogers worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and archaeology. He studied at the East India Company College from circa 1843 to 1845, and subsequently served in the Indian Civil Service from 1845 to 1879.

Alexander Rödel is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He earned a Master of Science by Research at the University of Edinburgh under the supervision of Steven Sutcliffe and Jeanne Openshaw (attested 2008).

Alexander Schiller works in Indology, history, and archaeology. He earned degrees from Appalachian State University, UC San Diego, and a PhD from Kansas State University in 2025, later becoming a Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

Aleksandr Aleksandrovich Stolyarov specializes in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied under Leonid B. Alaev, served as Director at the Russian State University for the Humanities (attested 2018), and is a senior research fellow at the Russian Academy of Sciences (attested 2026).
Alexander Studholme is a scholar in the field of Buddhist studies. Between circa 1996 and 2000, he studied under Paul Williams and Rupert Gethin.

Alexander W. Macdonald worked in Tibetology and religious studies. He served as a researcher at the CNRS from circa 1952 to 1989 and as a professor at Paris Nanterre University from circa 1971 to 1991.
Alexander Walker worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of St Andrews and served in the East India Company from circa 1780 to 1812.

Alexander Wynne specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Bristol and completed a DPhil at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich, serving as a Junior Research Fellow at St John's College, Oxford (2002–2006).

Alexander Yiannopoulos works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling and under numerous scholars and traditional teachers, including Karin Myers, Sherab Sangpo, Khenpo Sherab Dorje, and Georges B. J. Dreyfus.

Alexander Zieseniss was an Indologist who studied at Heidelberg, Freiburg, Tübingen, Berlin, and Hamburg, where he earned his PhD. He completed his Habilitation at the University of Hamburg (1936–1941) and served as Privatdozent at the University of Breslau (circa 1941–1945).

Alexander von Humboldt worked in history, archaeology, and other fields. He studied at Frankfurt (Oder), Göttingen, Handelsakademie Hamburg, TU Bergakademie Freiberg, and Jena, and later held a post at the University of Jena.

Alexander von Rospatt works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, and has held posts at the Nepal Research Centre, the University of Vienna, and the University of California, Berkeley.

Alexander von Staël-Holstein worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology. After studying at Tartu, Berlin, Halle (doctorate), and Saint Petersburg, he held professorships at Peking University and the Harvard-Yenching Institute, and directed the Sino-Indian Institute.
